questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How electric cars are designed and made
The UN climate change summit and its promises
Why factories cause so much air pollution
Low emission zones and how much they help the air
questions.why: Sam says they're discussing low emission zones, which aim to make the air we breathe cleaner.

questions.q: What happens to vehicles that don't meet emissions standards in London's zone?
options: They are taken away by the police and destroyed
Drivers must pay a daily charge or may be banned
They are only allowed to drive at night
Drivers receive a warning letter the first time
questions.why: Neil says drivers must pay a daily charge to drive in the zone, or might be banned altogether.

questions.q: What do these zones mainly target?
options: Smoke from factories on the edge of cities
Noise from heavy traffic in city centres
Poisonous exhaust gases from vehicles
Dust from building sites near schools
questions.why: Neil says they predominantly target exhaust fumes from vehicles, called nitrogen dioxide.

questions.q: According to Professor Alastair Lewis, what happens when pollution goes below the target level?
options: Health benefits continue to build up
There are no more health benefits
The air becomes too clean
Cities can stop measuring pollution
questions.why: He says we continue to see health benefits by reducing pollution, even below the target value.

questions.q: What is Professor Lewis's view of targets?
options: They are useless and a waste of government money
They should be set much higher than they are now
They are the only thing that matters in the end
They focus the mind but aren't the only thing to consider
questions.why: He says targets are very good at focusing the mind, but shouldn't be the only thing we consider.

questions.q: Why does Neil say there is more incentive to switch to electric cars in the UK?
options: Electric cars are now cheaper than petrol cars
Electric cars don't have to pay the daily charge
New diesel and petrol cars will be banned from 2040
Fuel prices have gone up a lot in the last year
questions.why: He says the government has said new diesel and petrol cars and vans will be banned from 2040.

questions.q: Why is air pollution a complex problem, according to Professor Lewis?
options: It has a very large number of different sources
Scientists still cannot measure it accurately
It only affects a few big cities like London
Most people don't believe it is really harmful
questions.why: He says it has a very large number of contributing sources, so no single action will cure it.

questions.q: What does Professor Lewis say about low emission zones on their own?
options: They will solve the problem completely
They are not the whole solution to air pollution
They make pollution worse
They should be removed
questions.why: He says they are one way to reduce concentrations but not, in isolation, the solution.
